title: Cohort Waterfall Matrix - Long Tail Investigation
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for a different lens on e2e tail: cohort-based waterfall matrix. Goal is to isolate which request cohorts (by seqlen, cache state, batch size, model variant, hw SKU) are dominating p95/p99 and whether the stage-level composition of their latency differs systematically from median requests.

Background / Motivation:
- We have many trace/playbooks about p99 paths and token-level tails. Those are useful but often mix cohorts together.
- Anecdotally some long-tail requests are not just longer in "emit" time but have disproportionately large upstream queueing or backend setup costs (cold KV, model variant swap, hw throttling).
- Idea: build a waterfall matrix: rows = cohorts, columns = pipeline stages (ingress, auth, routing, batch-wait, kernel-exec, kv-lookup, kv-restore, response-serialize, egress), cells show p50/p95/p99 for that stage within the cohort.

Dataset & filters used here (notes):
- Source traces: 2025-02-01 -> 2025-02-13 sampled traces from production (1% trace rate), enriched with request metadata (seqlen, kv_hit, batch_size, model_variant, hw_sku, warm/cold).
- Exclude synthetic/health-check routes and internal debug endpoints.
- Cohorts defined by cartesian grouping of: seqlen bucket (0-64, 65-256, 257-1024), kv_hit (hit/miss), batch_size (1, 2-8, >8), warm_flag (warm, cold), model_variant (v1, v1-quant, v2-ptq), hw_sku (A100-80GB, H100-80GB).
- For scale reasons we first union only cohorts with >= 250 traces in window; others grouped as "rare".

Methodology:
1) For each trace, compute per-stage duration. Stages: ingress (client->gateway), auth_check, route_lookup, prebatch_queue, batching_wait, backend_dispatch, kernel_exec, kv_lookup (if present), kv_restore, postproc, serialization, egress.
2) For each cohort, compute p50/p95/p99 of full e2e and of each stage.
3) Assemble a matrix: rows = cohorts (sorted by cohort p95 descending), cols = stages. Each cell: "p50 / p95 / p99 (ms)" for that stage.
4) Visual heuristics: highlight cells where stage_p99 >= 20% of cohort_p99. Those are strong contributors to tail. Also compute stage_share = stage_p99 / cohort_p99.

Sample matrix excerpt (text table) - top 6 cohorts by cohort_p95:

RowKey: seqlen|kv|batch|warm|model|hw | cohort_p50/p95/p99 (ms) | Ingress | Queue | Batch-wait | Kernel | KV | Serialize | Notes
1) 257-1024 | miss | 1 | cold | v1 | A100 | 420 / 1280 / 2560 | 5/10/20 | 12/30/70 | 40/110/220 | 210/700/1400 | 60/140/250 | 20/30/40 | Observed huge kernel and batch-wait contributor; kv adds noticeable tail
2) 65-256 | miss | 1 | warm | v1-quant | H100 | 180 / 640 / 1200 | 4/8/16 | 10/22/48 | 12/45/90 | 110/360/700 | 20/50/120 | 6/12/20 | Tail split between kernel and kv for misses
3) 0-64 | hit | >8 | warm | v2 | H100 | 60 / 220 / 540 | 3/6/10 | 8/18/30 | 4/9/18 | 18/40/120 | 2/4/6 | 3/6/9 | Batch >8: queue/batching small but kernel soft tail on v2
4) 257-1024 | hit | 2-8 | warm | v1 | A100 | 260 / 900 / 1800 | 5/12/25 | 20/55/110 | 15/40/80 | 150/520/1100 | 8/18/30 | 8/15/20 | Interesting: kernel still dominant but kv mostly hit so smaller contribution
5) 65-256 | miss | 2-8 | cold | v1 | A100 | 240 / 820 / 1500 | 4/9/18 | 18/40/90 | 25/70/150 | 125/420/900 | 40/120/240 | 6/12/18 | Cold + miss: kv+batching combine for tail
6) 0-64 | hit | 1 | cold | v1-quant | A100 | 80 / 300 / 650 | 5/10/18 | 8/22/48 | 6/14/32 | 30/110/300 | 2/4/8 | 5/10/15 | Small requests still get some heavy kv cold tail on p99

Preliminary findings / patterns:
- Kernel exec dominates absolute numbers for long-seqlen cohorts (expected), but for mid-seqlen (65-256) kv misses and batch-wait amplify the tail disproportionally.
- Cold requests with kv-miss frequently show a bi-modal tail: one mode where prebatch_queue/batch-wait is the large component (requests that waited to be batched then had heavy kernel), and another mode where kv_restore steps add long pauses (I/O / backend cold restore).
- Very large batches (>8) tend to sac downstream percentile but shift the p99 composition to kernel variability rather than queueing; suggests batching policy reduces queue but can exacerbate kernel variance.
- HW SKU differences: H100 cohorts show slightly lower kernel p95 but sometimes higher p99 due to micro-throttles (need to correlate with telemetry).

Hypotheses (ranked):
H1) KV cold-restore latency variance is causing a large fraction of mid-seqlen p95->p99 jump. Rehydration path needs TTL tuning and async prefetch for common prefixes.
H2) Our batching threshold heuristics create small cohorts that sit at <target latency but get occasionally stuck behind a heavy request, causing batch-wait spikes. Dynamic batch-splitting might help.
H3) Certain model_variant + quantization combos have non-linear kernel variance under mixed precision; this creates occasional long kernel stalls on large sequences.

Quick checks to run (quick TODOs):
- [ ] Correlate kv_restore traces with disk I/O metrics (EBS/NetIO) for the same time window (SRE ask: JIRA-7902).
- [ ] Run dedicated microbench for kv-restore with parallelism = 64 to reproduce tail (Noah to own).
- [ ] Instrument kernel-exec internal counters for memory compaction events and CUDA syncs for v1 vs v1-quant (Ethan).
- [ ] Recompute matrix with 2x higher trace sample from 2025-02-20 to capture weekend patterns.

Experiment ideas (small/medium/large):
- Small: Enable async kv-prefetch for requests that are cold but match recent hot-prefixes (feature flag). Measure cohort p99 change in 24h.
- Medium: Temporarily reduce max_batch_wait threshold for mid-seqlen cohorts during peak interval to see tail reduction. A/B by region.
- Large: Create a variant runtime image with split kernel scheduling to avoid single-hog kernels that block others (requires infra rollout).

Open questions / unknowns:
- How many p99 traces for mid-seqlen miss cohorts are repeat users vs random? If repeat, cache-warm strategies differ.
- Are KV restores correlated with pod restarts or eviction events? Need k8s evictions timeline overlay.
- Are heavy kernel p99 spikes correlated with multi-tenant noisy neighbors on dedicated nodes? Need instance-level telemetry.

Next steps / owners:
- Ethan: add kernel-exec internal counters and push small trace enrichment PR -> github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412 (link in artifacts). Target: 2025-03-07
- Noah: kv microbench and I/O correlation. Run initial bench by 2025-03-05.
- Sofia: create dashboard tile that displays waterfall-matrix heatmap per cohort (prototype in Grafana). 2025-03-09
- Maya (me): regenerate matrix with extended sample 2025-02-20->2025-03-01 and compare deltas.

Notes / loose thoughts:
- This matrix approach makes it easier to propose targeted mitigations per cohort rather than blanket fixes.
- We should save a canonical matrix snapshot per release (console UI idea) so PMs can see how rollouts affect specific cohorts.
- Could also overlay cost-per-request (ms * instance-cost) to find cost/perf sweet spots.

Links and references:
- Confluence primer (waterfall matrix): CONFLUENCE-2345
- Kernel variance investigation thread: slack://channels/serving-runtime-thread (refer to 2025-02-28 messages)
- Related Jira: JIRA-7891 (cohort-matrix epic), JIRA-7902 (kv IO correlation)

Immediate asks:
- If you have a quick script that maps traces -> cohort keys, paste here. I hacked a small SQL snippet but it's messy.
- Anyone who can run a 24h async prefetch experiment in staging please ping.

-- end of working doc (will convert to a polished playbook if findings hold).
